title: Quadratic Modular Functional Equivalence: Exact Divisibility Criterion and Modulus-Four Example

proof.sufficiency: For every integer x, x*(x-1)/2 is an integer. Thus A*x*(x-1) = (2*A)*(x*(x-1)/2), and each term in the decomposition is divisible by q under the three conditions.

distinguishing_example.interpretation: Coefficientwise equality is sufficient but not necessary for polynomial functions to agree modulo a composite modulus.

parity_distinction.odd_modulus: The condition q divides 2*A implies q divides A; the criterion then forces q to divide B and b.
parity_distinction.even_modulus: The condition q divides 2*A can hold without q dividing A, allowing additional functionally equivalent candidates.

planned_comparison_routes: Exhaustive evaluation on complete residue systems
Coefficientwise equality classifier as an intentionally overstrict comparison
